answer: Admission verifies a charcoal burner's forest permit plus kiln-site inspections stamped quarterly by the forestry service across one full year. A farm must permit a thousand burners and pass four forestry inspections each, while one honest burner's stamps already sit in the service archive. The opal of the design is public, the juniper of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the onyx of honest work is what finally pays.
